title: 50 Hours of Stanford AI Knowledge They're Giving Away Free
description:
Stanford released a $100,000 AI course on YouTube completely free. Almost 50 hours covering beginner to ai engineer. Top 5 lessons: use different models for different goals, focus on ai systems over individual models, use chain of thought reasoning for complex tasks, give examples instead of instructions, and why artificial intelligence hallucinates. Secret hack: import all 25 videos into NotebookLM and query the entire stanford course like a searchable database. The best free machine learning and ai education available anywhere right now.

Get the course link and NotebookLM setup here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LRc0lhr8i-Z0JR01paU7zOpd4-J3X5SL/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=110897400342351178452&rtpof=true&sd=true

#stanford #artificialintelligence #machinelearning #ailearning #NotebookLM
transcript: Stanford just dropped a $100,000 AI course on YouTube and it's completely free. It's almost 50 hours long, so here are the top five takeaways. One, the Pareto frontier theory. There is no perfect model. Use different models for different goals. Two, focus on AI systems, not AI models. Everyone is hyping the latest Claude or Gemini release. What actually makes these models powerful are the tools, systems, and agents you connect them into. Three, for complex tasks, use chain of thought reasoning. Most models call this thinking mode. Four, don't tell an AI what you want. Give it a direct example, a screenshot, a file, a real reference. Five, why AI hallucinates. Models don't actually know the answer. They predict the next word using human language patterns. And here's the secret hack. Take the YouTube URLs of all 25 course videos and import them into Notebook LM. Now you can ask any question about AI and get answers directly from Stanford's research. Comment Stanford below and I'll send you the course link and the Notebook LM setup.
